what_it_does: Every chip needs a power grid — a mesh of metal wires that delivers electricity from the pins to every logic gate on the die. At cutting-edge process nodes (3 nm and 2 nm, referring to the size of transistors), designing that grid is extremely complex: a poor layout causes voltage drops that slow down or crash the chip, while an over-engineered grid wastes area and power. This paper frames power-grid design as a search problem and proposes an automated framework that generates candidate grid topologies as sequences (like words in a sentence) and then scores them using a Transformer-based model (the same attention-based architecture behind large language models) that predicts how much voltage will drop across the grid. The model's learned internal representations are used to find grid designs on the 'Pareto frontier' — the set of options where you cannot improve voltage integrity without increasing cost, or vice versa.
